name: GPS (Global Positioning System)
tagline: The original GNSS — 31 satellites, free public service since 2000
description: Global Positioning System — the original GNSS and still the most widely used. 31 active satellites at 20,180 km in 6 orbital planes inclined 55°. Operated by US Space Force; originally Department of Defense. President Reagan's 1983 directive promised future civilian GPS access after the Korean Air Lines 007 shootdown, but civilian unencrypted L1 C/A signal access was not available until Selective Availability was turned off in May 2000, dramatically improving civilian accuracy. Modernised L1C, L2C, L5 signals on Block IIF and III satellites.
best_known_for: The original GNSS — 31 satellites, free public service since 2000
